items.entity: rectangular design domain (side lengths / aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that the beam is rectangular and that 'the boundary conditions and structural dimensions are illustrated in Figure 8(a)'. The text gives no side lengths, units or aspect ratio.

items.entity: which side of the rectangle is the long side
items.description: Sec. 4.1: 'The beam has a rectangular shape, with its width greater than its length.' This contradicts the usual beam convention (length = span), so it is unclear whether the horizontal span between the clamped left/right edges is longer or shorter than the vertical height.
readings: horizontal span (between clamped left/right edges) > vertical height (usual slender clamped-clamped beam)
vertical height > horizontal span (tall/deep domain, if 'length' means the clamp-to-clamp span)

items.description: Sec. 4.1: 'A horizontally downward force is applied at the top center.' 'Horizontally' and 'downward' contradict each other.
readings: horizontal (+x or -x; mirror images of each other)
inclined, with both horizontal and downward components (e.g. 45 degrees)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'applied at the top center' and refers to Fig. 8(a) for the boundary conditions. It does not say whether the load acts at a single node or as a traction over a short segment of the top edge, or how wide that segment is.
readings: concentrated point load at the top-edge mid node
load split equally over the 2-3 nodes nearest the mid-point
uniform traction over a short centered segment of the top edge (about 2-5% of the span)

items.description: The text gives no force value. Secs. 4.2.1/4.3.1 say the low-fidelity initial designs use a different force magnitude (and material) from the high-fidelity model and that this is 'the same with double clamper beam case'. Any values appear only in Fig. 8(a).
readings: low-fidelity force value shown in Fig. 8(a)
high-fidelity (COMSOL) force value shown in Fig. 8(a)

items.entity: V0 values of the 160 designs per Lmin
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1: '160 different solutions by varying the V0 from 0.25 to 0.50'. The sampling scheme is not stated (spacing, whether endpoints are included, deterministic or random).

items.entity: V0 of the 15 representative designs in Fig. 8(b)
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says only 'five structures for each Lmin, arranged in increasing volume fraction order'. Their V0 values are not in the text. It is also unclear whether any volume labels in the figure are the low-fidelity V0 or the de-homogenized high-fidelity volume (volumes reported elsewhere, e.g. about 0.21-0.29 in Sec. 4.1.4, are high-fidelity values that need not equal V0).
readings: values read off Fig. 8(b), possibly high-fidelity volumes rather than V0

items.entity: volume measure V(mu1, mu2, rho) in Eq. (33)
items.description: Eq. (33) imposes V(mu1, mu2, rho) <= V0 but never defines V for the cross-shaped cell with widths mu1*rho, mu2*rho (Eq. 32). This decides which solid area fraction a single-material solver should impose to match V0.
readings: V = mean of (mu1*rho + mu2*rho - mu1*mu2*rho^2), the true solid fraction of the cross cell, so single-material volume fraction = V0
V = mean of rho*(mu1 + mu2 - mu1*mu2)
V = mean of (mu1*rho + mu2*rho), overlap counted twice, so the true solid fraction is below V0

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1/Eq. (33): Lmin is a lower bound on the dimensionless bar widths mu1, mu2 of the cross microstructure (relative to the unit cell), yet it is called a 'minimum feature size'. It has no direct counterpart in a single-material solver, and its relation to a physical length or element size is not given. It does change the layout: larger Lmin gives more large internal voids.
readings: ignore Lmin (one design per V0 instead of three)
minimum length scale / filter radius = Lmin x domain height (0.1H, 0.15H, 0.2H)
minimum length scale = Lmin x macro-element size (sub-element, so effectively no length-scale control)

items.entity: upper bounds Lmax and rho_max in Eq. (33)
items.description: Eq. (33) uses Lmax and rho_max without values (Sec. 4.1.1 only states rho in [0,1]). If Lmax < 1, no fully solid cell is possible and the maximum element stiffness stays below that of the base material.
readings: Lmax = 1, rho_max = 1 (fully solid elements allowed; single-material rho_max = 1)

items.description: rho_min in Eq. (33) is not given, and the residual stiffness of the polynomial fit C^H (Eq. 4) at near-zero bar widths is unknown. A single-material solver needs an ersatz Emin or minimum density.

items.entity: material interpolation / penalization of macroscopic density rho
items.description: Eq. (31) puts rho into C^H(mu1*rho, mu2*rho) with no penalty exponent or projection, although rho is meant to separate void from lattice-filled regions (Sec. 4.1.1). The interpolation a single-material solver should use, and how intermediate 'lattice' densities are treated, is not specified. The parameters of the SIMP comparison designs (Dsg.4, code [49], Sec. 4.1.4) are not reported either.
readings: no penalization, p = 1 (intermediate densities stand in for lattice infill)
p continuation 1 to 3 and/or Heaviside projection with beta continuation
use the homogenized cross-cell stiffness curve C^H(rho, rho) as the interpolation

items.description: Secs. 3.2 and 4.1.1 mention no density or sensitivity filter, filter radius or projection for the low-fidelity optimization.

The update scheme, move limit, iteration limit and convergence tolerance for the low-fidelity optimization (Eq. 33) are not given. Only the benchmark codes [48], [49] are cited, and only for the comparison designs.
readings: MMA, move limit 0.2, max 300 iterations, change tolerance 0.01
OC, move limit 0.2, damping 0.5, change tolerance 0.01

items.description: The initial values of rho, mu1, mu2 and theta for the 480 low-fidelity runs are not stated. The problem is non-convex, so the starting point can change the result.
readings: uniform rho = 1 with mu1 = mu2 chosen to meet V0 and theta = 0
theta initialized from principal stress directions of a solid analysis

items.description: The number of macro elements N_m, element size and element type for this example are never given (Sec. 2.2.1 only names coarse, intermediate and fine meshes). It is also unclear whether a single-material re-run should use the coarse homogenization grid or a fine single-scale grid.
readings: fine single-scale grid, e.g. 600 x 300 Q4 elements

items.description: Only E = 1 and nu = 0.3 for the base material are given (Sec. 3.2). Plane stress vs. plane strain is not stated, and the choice changes the effective Poisson's ratio.
readings: plane strain (effective nu about 0.43, E' = E/(1 - nu^2))

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2D model, low- or high-fidelity.

Eqs. (22)/(33) leave obj generic, and Sec. 3.2 says only 'stiffness optimization'. The stiffness metric used later in the high-fidelity stage (Sec. 4.1.2) is maximum displacement, so compliance is implied but not stated.
readings: displacement at the load point in the load direction

items.description: The text never mentions passive regions. Whether the whole rectangle is designable (or has, e.g., a solid pad under the load or along the clamps) is shown only as 'the design space' in Fig. 8(a).
readings: small solid non-design pad under the top-center load
thin solid non-design strips along the clamped left/right edges

locator: Sec. 4.1.1, the double-clamped beam, low-fidelity stiffness designs (Fig. 8)
